$comment: Single definition of the security-review vulnerability taxonomy. categories are the display names a report may show. slugs maps every canonical category slug to its display name. The first segment of a finding's ruleId must be one of these slugs.

categories.name: Access Controls
categories.description: Authorization, ownership, and privilege boundaries that limit what an identity can read, change, or execute.

categories.name: Auditing and Logging
categories.description: Security event records, traceability, log integrity, monitoring signals, and support for incident response.

categories.name: Authentication
categories.description: Identity verification, credentials, account recovery, multi-factor controls, and login protections.

categories.name: Configuration
categories.description: Security-sensitive defaults, deployment settings, dependency controls, and operational hardening.

categories.name: Cryptography
categories.description: Encryption, hashing, random values, key handling, certificate validation, and protected transport.

categories.name: Data Exposure
categories.description: Unintended disclosure through storage, logs, interfaces, metadata, temporary files, or error responses.

categories.name: Data Validation
categories.description: Checks and transformations applied before untrusted data reaches commands, queries, files, URLs, or templates.

categories.name: Denial of Service
categories.description: Conditions that can exhaust resources, block useful work, or reduce service availability.

categories.name: Error Reporting
categories.description: Failure handling and messages that can expose internal details or prevent safe diagnosis.

categories.name: Session Management
categories.description: Session creation, storage, rotation, expiration, revocation, and binding to an authenticated identity.

categories.name: Timing
categories.description: Race conditions, time-of-check/time-of-use gaps, and observable timing differences.

categories.name: Undefined Behavior
categories.description: Memory, language, or runtime behavior that can produce unsafe results outside intended program rules.
